title: A schedule across the family’s devices
description: One person builds the sequence in pictures, another carries it out on their own device. Edits and check-ins are available to the participants who were chosen.

blocks.text: A parent prepared the schedule, but it never appeared on the child’s device. The family has to move the pictures and the steps across all over again. When life is split between several homes, it also matters to know which version of the plan is in force today.

quote.text: you can’t share/sync the schedules you create, which pretty much makes it a nuisance to use if your kids have their own phones/iPads. My kids also have days at their dads house so I can’t check on their progress while they aren’t at my house.

blocks.text: Store a separate plan for each participant and grant access to the adults who need it. Show the time of the last update on every device. Changing the future schedule must not erase steps already completed; a temporary loss of connection has to be visible.

Prepare a single day on an adult’s phone and open it on another device. Then change a step and check both sides. The value here is shared access and the plan staying intact; how convenient the visual schedule is has to be judged with a particular family.
